author: opus-5.5
body:
[opus 5.5] Cause found; fix approved for implementation, not yet built or deployed.

The short reads after a cut are caused by the history the voice service re-seeds into the fresh backend session. After a few cuts that history holds several read requests, each paired with an assistant reply of only a few words, and the model imitates those replies on the next read. Neither the prompt nor any other session state is responsible.

Controlled probe against the deployed backend, with neutral stand-in text, the production instructions and the production read-prompt template. 3 trials per variant; every response ended normally.
- Current seed: 1/3 full, in both a fresh-message set and a set that re-reads the seeded message as production does.
- Seed without any assistant items: 6/6 full (3/3 exact in the re-read set).
- Only the last pair or two seeded: 6/6 full.
- No seed: 3/3 full.
- Cut replies marked as interrupted: 1/3. Cut replies reworded as a description: 0/3, because the model copied the description.
- A seed that also held a completed few-word reply: 2/3. A completed short read can trigger this as well as a cut one, so skipping only cut replies is not enough.

Fix approved for implementation: after a renewal, seed only the user's turns. Known limit: a renewed session keeps the user's earlier turns but not the assistant's own earlier replies. Continuity questions about a message still work, because the message text is part of the user's read request; the deploy acceptance re-checks this.

Remaining: implement with tests, review, a single rollout, then a live re-check of reads after a cut plus the full latency and continuity suite.
